message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted maximum, but drivers must still obey “reasonable and prudent” speed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.021–545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is a moving‑violation offense. | Texas Transportation Code §545.025 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights, stop signs, and yield signs.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• “Yield to emergency vehicles” when sirens are active. | Texas Transportation Code §545.030 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code §545.040 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.050 | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop sign extended. | Texas Transportation Code §545.060 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.070 | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or abandoned.
• Towing a vehicle without proper authorization can lead to penalties. | Texas Transportation Code §545.080 | | **Driving Under the Influence of Drugs** | • Prescription drugs that impair driving are treated similarly to alcohol. | Texas Transportation Code §545.090 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Official rules, forms, and updates. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/ 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. *Online:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings. 4. **Texas Highway Patrol** – Enforcement and public safety advisories. *Website:* https://www.txdps.state.tx.us/highwaypatrol/ --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a simple rule that saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone away or use hands‑free. - **Know your speed limit** – especially on rural roads where limits can be higher. - **Respect school buses** – they’re there to protect children. - **Check your vehicle’s registration and inspection status** – avoid fines and keep your car safe. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper details on any specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, parking regulations, or how to register a vehicle).
